seo_title: Cost of Living in Kutaisi 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Kutaisi per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A quiet alternative to Tbilisi: the same 365 days visa-free, even lower prices, with mountains and canyons nearby. The Wizz Air low-cost hub makes the city a convenient base for travelling around Europe.
pros: Visa-free entry for 365 days — just like Tbilisi
Prices are even lower than in Tbilisi and Batumi
A Wizz Air hub — cheap flights to Europe
A 'Small Business' sole proprietorship with a 1% tax
Close to mountains, canyons and the Prometheus Cave
cons: A small city with limited infrastructure
A weaker IT community than in Tbilisi
Few international schools and little quality private healthcare
A modest selection of restaurants and shops

best_places.name: Bagrati Cathedral
best_places.description: A UNESCO site on a hill with a panorama of the city and a view of the mountains.

best_places.name: Kutaisi Airport
best_places.description: A Wizz Air hub: cheap flights to Europe — Budapest, Warsaw, Berlin, Rome.

best_places.name: Pheasant's Tears
best_places.description: A wine restaurant of the local school — natural Georgian wines and seasonal cuisine.

best_places.name: Okatse Canyon
best_places.description: Suspension bridges over the canyon an hour's drive away — the region's most beautiful spot.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 365 days without a visa — all you need is a passport; the stamp is issued at the border.

visa_steps.title: Personal Number (ID)
visa_steps.description: Get one at the House of Justice in Kutaisi — needed for renting, banking and sole proprietorship.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Bank of Georgia, TBC and Liberty Bank open accounts for Russians in Kutaisi.

visa_steps.title: 'Small Business' sole proprietorship
visa_steps.description: A 1% tax with turnover up to 500,000 GEL, set up in a day at RS.ge.

visa_steps.title: Registered rental
visa_steps.description: The lease is recorded in the registry; the market is small — start looking early.

faq.question: How is Kutaisi different from Tbilisi?
faq.answer: Cheaper, quieter, closer to the mountains and the low-cost airport. But there's less of an IT scene and fewer amenities.

faq.question: What about banks in Kutaisi?
faq.answer: Bank of Georgia and TBC are the main ones. The terms are the same as in Tbilisi.

faq.question: Can I fly to Europe?
faq.answer: Yes, Kutaisi Airport is the main Wizz Air hub in the region. Tickets from 30 €.

faq.question: What about healthcare in Kutaisi?
faq.answer: There's a private clinic, MediClub, but for complex cases many go to Tbilisi.

faq.question: What about families with children in Kutaisi?
faq.answer: There are no international schools, but there are good local and online options.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Kutaisi?
faq.answer: Humid subtropical: +12°C in winter, +28°C in summer, with plenty of rainfall.

reviews.text: I moved over from Tbilisi: rent is 1.5 times cheaper, the airport is 20 minutes away, and Europe is a 30 € flight. The downside — fewer cafés and groceries to choose from.
Kutaisi is for those who want quiet and a convenient travel hub. It's not a tourist city, it's a working base.
